# BSC (Bharat Steel Group) — Sales Call Knowledge Base (auto-distilled)

## Corpus summary

This corpus is a mixed bag of **hundreds of short call snippets**, and only a modest fraction are genuine sales/trade conversations. A large portion of the transcripts are **not usable for sales training**: internal MTC/tag/TC paperwork chasing (Site Vinoth calls), driver/loading/crane logistics, payment-charges disputes, garbled personal/Hindi-Tamil chatter (Vishal, Veer threads – clearly unrelated personal calls, possibly wrong numbers), voicemails, and one-line "wrong number" calls. Even among the real sales calls, most are **very short, transactional check-ins** (rate confirmation, stock check, delivery date, payment status) rather than full consultative sales pitches. There are few long-form objection-handling or closing conversations; most "negotiation" is a single round of rate-haggling (±₹500–₹2000/ton) before the customer agrees or defers. Given this, the KB below is built strictly from the recurring patterns actually visible: TMT/structural steel/sheet-plate trading, rate-citation by brand/location, MTC-tag compliance, and short counter-offers. Findings should be read as directional, not exhaustive — the sample is thin on deep objection-handling dialogue.

## Products & brand ladder

Based on actual mentions, BSC trades (not manufactures in most cases) a **structural & flat steel basket**, sourced from large mills and resold/cut-to-size:

- **TMT Rebar** – grades **Fe 500, 500D, 550D** discussed. Noted: "500 stop பண்ணிட்டாங்களா... 500 வெறும் R&L தான் produce பண்ணுவாங்க... 550D தான் sir வரும்." Brands: **Sail (CRS/sale), Vizag (RINL), Tata**. CRS pipe note: "sale TMT 500D தான் வருமா sir CRS-ல? ஆ CRS-ல 500D தான் sir வரும்... 550 வராது."
- **Structural steel**: ISMB (I-beam), ISMC/channel, angle (L angle, 90x90, 100x100), SHS/square pipe, rectangle pipe, flats (various widths/thickness), round bars. "ISMB அதே தான் sir எல்லாமே 65 range தான்."
- **Plates/Sheets**: MS plate, checkered plate, CR coil/sheet (0.6mm CRCA mentioned), standard sizes **2500x6300mm / "2.5 to 6300" is the stock norm**; coil-cutting available but with minimum/lead-time constraints.
- **Brands cited**: Tata Steel, Sail/CRS, Vizag/RINL, Vaisakh (Visakhapatnam), Apollo (pipes – "local make"), NMDC (plates), JSW (price-mover referenced). Distinction made repeatedly: "Vaisakh-க்கும் sale-க்கும் difference இருக்கா rate-ல? Rate different இருக்காது sir. ரெண்டுமே same price தான்."
- **Brand-ladder logic**: Tata = premium/high rate but often *unavailable in smaller thickness*; Sail/Vizag = standard default; local/unbranded = cheapest, used when branded stock unavailable ("2.5mm-ல வேணும்னா local brand-ல கிடைக்கும்... Apollo check பண்ணனும்").
- Grade/spec distinctions matter to buyers: grade 250 vs E350 ("E350-ன்னா உங்களுக்கு அதோட ₹3000 extra வரும்"), thickness tolerance disputes (2.5mm ordered vs 2.6/2.9mm supplied causing weight/billing friction with customers).

## Real rates & terms (only rates that actually appear in the calls)

- ISMB/MS round: **₹65–70/kg range**, Vizag-sourced MS round ≈ **₹68**.
- Sheet/plate (8mm, various): **₹59.5–61.5/kg** early in period, rising to **₹63–67/kg** later (clear upward trend referenced repeatedly: "rate ஜாஸ்தியா போயிட்டு இருக்கு", "₹1500 increase ஆகும்னு சொல்றாங்க").
- Flat 300x140 vs 300x150 ISMC comparison: **₹60 vs ₹63/kg**, weight difference 42 vs 46 kg/meter, used as a trade-off pitch ("option குடுக்குறேன்... rate ₹3000 கம்மியாக கிடைக்குது").
- TMT/structural quote example: **₹69/kg (12mm), ₹68.5/kg (16mm)**, GST extra.
- CRS 20mm sale rate: **₹69,000** (per ton, "sale CRS... that's the only available item").
- Checkered/plate rates: 6mm plate **₹66/kg + GST**; 8mm/5mm plate **₹63.5–64/kg**; 2mm plate **₹63/kg**; general plate band **₹61–62/kg**.
- Vizag TMT rates (regional comparables cited by a distributor): **₹62,000–65,500/ton**, with ₹500–1000 regional premiums for 8–12mm.
- Transport/logistics charges (ancillary, not product rate but quoted in calls): **₹1200/ton transport (min 10–14 ton load)**; **Payment/handling charge standardised at ₹200**, disputed when billed at ₹250; trailer rentals for long flats ₹15,000; inter-city freight quotes ₹1800–2150/trip (Dushyant transport calls).
- Standard commercial terms repeatedly seen: **"GST + loading + transport extra"** on every basic rate quoted; **quotation validity typically "2 days"**; advance/full payment commonly required before dispatch ("Full payment இருந்தாதான் block பண்ண முடியும்"); **Cash & Carry** is a distinct (slightly lower) rate tier offered to some customers.
- Credit terms exist but are capped: "1 month தான் credit" and even then rate is fixed at time of invoice, not negotiable retroactively.

## Objection Playbook

**1. "Rate too high / competitor cheaper"**
- Customer: "Tata Steel ₹60-க்கு வாங்கினேனுமா நேத்துக்கு?" 
- Response pattern: differentiate by item/spec, not blanket match — "இந்த 1 item வந்து அதிகமா இருக்கு cost... Joyster brand தான் இப்ப வந்து cost கூட இருக்கு."
- When pushed on discount: hold firm citing mill-level price control — "loading charges கூட கம்மி பண்ண முடியாது sir... rate correct-ஆ தான் இருக்கு."

**2. "Give me at least ₹X off / old customer loyalty ask"**
- Common counter: offer a **small, bounded concession** (₹500–₹1000, or switch to Cash & Carry tier) rather than open negotiation — "Cash and Carry ₹500 நீங்க 10-க்கு try பண்ணலாம்." If margin truly fixed: "நான் increase பண்ணி கொடுத்துட்டு கம்மி பண்ணலைன்னா அது மாதிரி பண்ண மாட்டோம்."

**3. Spec/thickness substitution pushback**
- When exact thickness unavailable (e.g., 2.5mm out of stock), rep offers nearest available with honesty about cost impact: "2.5mm stock இல்ல... 2.6, 2.9 போட்டுருக்கேன்... weight difference வந்து எங்களுக்கு காசு கொடுக்க மாட்டாங்க." Customer pushes back on wastage cost — rep must escalate to mill/distributor before confirming.

**4. Billing/charges disputes (payment charge, transport add-on surprise)**
- Standard move: acknowledge as "mistake," offer a **debit/credit note** rather than editing the live invoice (e-way bill constraints): "அது நான் debit note raise பண்ணிடுறேன்... invoice cancel பண்ண முடியாது sir, e-way bill போட்டாச்சு."

**5. Payment-before-dispatch standoff**
- Customers often want material moved before full payment clears; BSC's firm line: "Full payment இருந்தாதான் block பண்ண முடியும்," though partial advance + rate-lock is sometimes offered: "advance பண்ணி block பண்ணிக்கிறேன்னா I can give...".

**6. "Will rate reduce if I wait?"**
- Honest, non-committal answer pattern, leaning cautious: "ரொம்ப high-ல இருக்கு... increase ஆகுற chances இப்ப கம்மி... but கம்மி ஆகுமான்னு chances இருக்கு." Advice given to customers to buy **limited/urgent-only quantity** rather than stockpile in a volatile market.

## Effective Lines (openings, discovery, closing, follow-up)

**Openings**
- "சார் சொல்லுங்க சார்." / "Good morning sir, சொல்லுங்க sir." — simple, fast, no fluff; let the caller state need immediately.
- Identify self and account context quickly: "Narendra பேசுறேன் Sir, இங்க Aster-ல இருந்து."

**Discovery**
- Quantity + spec drilldown is immediate and specific: "என்ன quantity வேணும்? என்ன thickness? Grade 250-மா?"
- Clarify delivery location early, since transport is a separate cost line: "Delivery எங்க sir? Chennai-தான்? எங்க exact location?"

**Closing nudges**
- Bundling a small concession with urgency: "Okay-ன்னா நான் PO அனுப்பிச்சிடுறேன்."
- Creating gentle urgency around price trend: "rate increase ஆக போகுது... quantity ஏதாவது confirm பண்ணுங்க."
- Offering to "check and get back" rather than over-promising live on call — very common, builds trust without overcommitting: "நான் check பண்ணிட்டு சொல்றேன்."

**Follow-up**
- Proactive rate-sharing via WhatsApp/mail after calls is standard and expected: "நான் rate அனுப்புறேன் WhatsApp-ல."
- Confirming receipt and status loops tightly: "அனுப்பிச்சிட்டீங்களா? Okay நான் பார்க்கிறேன்."

## Common Call Scenarios

1. **Rate enquiry / price check** — by far the most frequent call type: customer asks "இன்னைக்கு rate என்ன?" for TMT, plate, ISMB, flat etc.; rep quotes base rate + "GST/loading/transport extra."
2. **Stock/availability check** — "material available-ஆ இருக்கா?", frequently followed by thickness/size mismatch resolution (coil-cut lead times, "நாளைக்கு தான் கிடைக்கும்").
3. **Quotation negotiation** — customer asks for small discount; rep holds firm or offers narrow concession, cites mill-level pricing constraints.
4. **Order confirmation & payment coordination** — PO/payment status chasing, advance vs full payment, UTR/bank confirmation calls.
